incidentTests.title: Incident A variants — setup retry and dispatch ambiguity
incidentTests.intent: Inject transient and permanent setup failures, dispatch-accepted followed by ledger-write-failure, duplicate queue messages
incidentTests.assertions: No duplicate execution; dispatch_uncertain recorded; DLQ custody on exhaustion; setup stage checkpoints persist

incidentTests.title: Incident B — conversation continuity
incidentTests.intent: Health/help queries and same-conversation replies to active and terminal tasks
incidentTests.assertions: Health queries pass without /task; terminal-task 'where is the output' triggers controlled resend; cross-conversation denied

incidentTests.title: Incident C — result validation and delivery
incidentTests.intent: Completion with only a summary; Telegram send failures; provider acceptance recording
incidentTests.assertions: Completion rejected without canonical result; persisted result exists before any send; failed sends set retry_wait/unknown_after_send

incidentTests.title: Incident D — prior output recovery
incidentTests.intent: Repair/replay requests mapped to latest same-conversation task
incidentTests.assertions: Resend reads task_results; zero Flue/Sandbox/model calls; idempotent delivery

props.content: Keep the current stack. The next release must persist the canonical result, create a durable delivery intent, and preserve Telegram acceptance or ambiguity before declaring success.

### Verdict

Keep the current stack; do not rewrite the runtime. Failures are application-layer contract gaps (result persistence, outbox, delivery, routing). See recommended Phase 0 changes.

### Top operational blockers

1) No durable general result; 2) No outbound outbox; 3) Completion conflates execution & delivery; 4) Scratch-only artifacts; 5) Command-only routing.

props.caption: Recommended minimal architecture: persist result before sending; send from durable outbox; record provider acceptance or ambiguity.

props.content: Additive tables (keep old fields): task_results — canonical per-task result versions; task_delivery — per-channel delivery records and states; task_stage_attempts — stage-scoped attempt records. Invariants: (task_id, result_version) unique; persist result before advancing legacy completed state; delivery rows never delete results.

### Risks & non-goals

Do not migrate to a second runtime. Preserve allowlists, DO migration compatibility, activity redaction, and write-token separation. A DLQ helps diagnostics but is not a substitute for result/state invariants.
